questions.question: Why is `<button onClick={...}>` preferred over `<div onClick={...}>` for a clickable action?
options: Divs cannot have onClick handlers at all
A native button is focusable and keyboard-activatable (Enter/Space) and is announced correctly by screen readers, without extra code
It's purely a stylistic convention with no functional difference
questions.explanation: A div requires manually adding tabIndex, keydown handling, and a role to match what a native button provides automatically.

questions.question: When should you reach for an ARIA attribute like `aria-expanded`?
options: On every element, as a best practice
To describe state or relationships that semantic HTML alone can't express, such as whether a collapsible section is open
Instead of using semantic HTML elements
questions.explanation: ARIA should supplement semantic HTML for cases HTML can't express alone, not replace choosing the correct element in the first place.

questions.question: What should happen to keyboard focus when a modal dialog closes?
options: Nothing — focus state doesn't matter for modals
Focus should return to whatever element triggered the modal, so it isn't lost behind the now-hidden content
Focus should move to the top of the page
questions.explanation: Without returning focus to the trigger, a keyboard user loses their place entirely once the modal (which held focus) disappears.

questions.question: What does a tool like `jest-axe` actually verify, and what does it NOT replace?
options: It fully replaces manual keyboard and screen-reader testing
It automatically catches a subset of issues like missing labels and invalid ARIA usage in CI, but doesn't replace manual keyboard/screen-reader testing
It only checks color contrast and nothing else
questions.explanation: Automated accessibility checks catch cheap regressions (missing aria-label, contrast issues) but can't verify the full experience of navigating with a keyboard or screen reader.
